reason: The fragments' knobs match a lymphocyte's recognition proteins, and the intro says this encounter helps activate it.
expectation: The matching lymphocyte will be activated, or prepared for activation, after recognizing the bacterial fragments.

effect: The matching lymphocyte is active; the intro says the lymph node supports its descendants multiplying.
reaction: The matching shapes made the activation understandable.
reason: The lymph node is described as supporting activated cells as they multiply, so it is the next place to use the lymphocyte.
expectation: The activated lymphocyte will multiply in the lymph node, leading toward antibody-producing and memory cells.

effect: The lymph node produced antibody-making cells and memory cells; the remaining goal is to help clear the bacteria.
reaction: The split between making antibodies now and keeping memory cells is clear.
reason: Antibodies are proteins, and amino acids are protein building blocks, so the antibody-making cells may use them.
expectation: The cells will make antibodies that match the bacterial antigens.

effect: The cells made matching antibodies from amino acids; their tips fit the bacteria's surface knobs.
reaction: The matching shapes make the next connection clear.
reason: The antibodies' tips match the knobs on the bacteria, so they should bind to them.
expectation: The antibodies will coat the bacteria, helping the engulfing white blood cells recognize them.

effect: The antibodies coated the bacteria, leaving them ready for engulfing white blood cells.
reaction: The coating matches the white blood cell picture, making the next step clear.
reason: The white blood cells can bind to the outward-facing parts of antibodies and engulf the coated bacteria.
expectation: The white blood cells will engulf the coated bacteria and help clear them.

effect: The white blood cells engulfed and broke down the coated bacteria, completing the remaining goal.
reaction: It was satisfying to see how the antibody coating helped the cells clear the bacteria.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making the antibody-producing and memory cells was most worthwhile: it showed how one response can both act now and leave memory cells behind.

leastWorthwhile.text: Making the antibodies was a fairly predictable use of amino acids, so it was less interesting than seeing what the antibodies did.

surprise.text: The antibodies marked bacteria for other white blood cells to engulf, rather than clearing them on their own.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt especially arbitrary; the pictures and introduction made the pairings understandable.

continue.text: I would continue to see how memory cells help in a later response. This chapter introduced them but ended before showing that.
